subject: Residency & retention alignment for CloudLytics marketplace listing
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@cloudlytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Residency & retention questions for marketplace listing

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — CloudLytics is excited to move forward with the Redwood marketplace listing. Before we finalize the technical docs for the listing we need to confirm a few items related to data residency, retention, and deletion across AWS/GCP/Azure. Our procurement and legal teams want clear answers for buyers. Quick questions below — can you confirm: 

1) For customers who select a particular cloud region (AWS us-east-1 / GCP us-central1 / Azure eastus), does Redwood guarantee all inference input (prompts) and KV-cache materialize only in that region, or are there any control-plane hops outside the region we should call out?

2) What's your default retention window for request/response logs versus short-term cache (KV cache/prefix cache)? Can customers set per-account overrides in the marketplace flow?

3) If a buyer requests complete deletion, what is the SLA and the deletion scope (S3 blobs, DB rows, audit logs, backups)? Also, how do you handle cross-cloud backups or multi-region replication?

I'll attach the list our legal team compiled. Happy to hop on a short call if it's easier.

Thanks,
Sophie
Head of Partnerships
CloudLytics Inc.

Attachment: CloudLytics-questions.pdf (pdf)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@cloudlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Residency & retention questions for marketplace listing

Hi Sophie — thanks, and great to hear you're moving forward. Looping Marissa (security/compliance) and Ben (partner ops) since they own parts of this. Below are short answers; I'll follow up with a one-page summary and the mappings we use for marketplace listings.

1) Residency and control-plane hops:
- Inference inputs and KV cache are hosted in the customer-selected region for the serving runtime (we pin inference workers to the region/GCP zone/Azure region).
- Control-plane operations (scheduling, billing metadata, model catalog) are handled by Redwood control plane. For Redwood Private customers we can offer a VPC-connected control plane; for Hosted/Dedicated marketplace listings the minimal control-plane metadata (tenant id, billing usage counters) may transit our control plane in the US. No plaintext content is routed through the control plane — only metadata and encrypted pointers.

2) Retention windows:
- Default request/response audit logs: 90 days (configurable to shorter windows for Marketplace listings via a per-account policy).
- KV/prefix cache: ephemeral by design — TTL defaults to 1 hour for most models; we persist only what customers opt into for longer caching.
- Customers can request per-account overrides at onboarding; we capture those in the Marketplace onboarding payload and enforce via account policy.

3) Deletion SLA and scope:
- Deletion request SLA: standard is 7 business days for a full scoped delete (includes blobs, primary DB records, and visible audit logs).
- Backups: we remove primary data and mark backups for deletion; final scrub of immutable backups occurs on the next retention-cycle which is no longer than 30 days. We document the backup window in the Marketplace listing if extended retention or cross-region replication is enabled.

I've attached the residency mapping workbook we use for marketplace docs — it shows which artifacts live where and which controls apply per cloud. Ben — can you confirm whether we need to add any marketplace-specific wording for cross-cloud replication on the listing? Marissa — any compliance caveats to add for the doc?

Best,
Markus
Senior Partner Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: residency_mapping_v2.xlsx (xlsx)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mark us Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@cloudlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Residency & retention questions for marketplace listing

Thanks Markus — quick clarifications from ops side: 
- Marketplace listing: we will surface the "Data residency: customer-selected region" statement. For any partner that enables cross-cloud failover/replication we must show the failover region and retention implications explicitly.
- Onboarding payload allows a boolean flag: enforce_short_retention=true and preferred_retention_days (min:7, default:90). Marketplace UI will expose these during checkout for enterprise buyers.
- For deletion, ops executes a two-phase flow: immediate logical delete + audit entry, then physical purge during next maintenance window (we aim <30 days, typically within 7-10 days for Marketplace deals unless account opts into extended snapshotting).

Sophie — if CloudLytics requires an expedited deletion (e.g., regulatory hold), we can accept an escalation via the partner portal and tag the account for priority purge. We can put the escalation process into the partner playbook.

Cheers,
Ben
Partner Operations
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@cloudlytics.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T13:50:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Residency & retention questions for marketplace listing

Hi Sophie — security notes to include in the listing and the short FAQ: 
- Encryption: All at-rest data stores (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) use customer-isolated buckets/containers when requested; keys are customer-managed via KMS/HSM where the buyer requests Bring-Your-Own-Key.
- Control-plane metadata: as Markus said, no plaintext PII is sent to Redwood control plane — only hashed tenant IDs and usage counters. Call out that model artifacts may be cached briefly in the serving region for efficiency.
- Audit logs: we retain admin audit trails for operational debugging for up to 180 days per our internal policy; however, we can exclude customer application payloads from audit retention if a marketable "no-payload retention" option is selected.

Action items for the listing:
- Add a one-paragraph FAQ "What data leaves the selected region?" — short answer: only encrypted control-plane metadata and non-PII metrics.
- Add explicit deletion SLA language and backup-window expectations (7–30 days depending on backup snapshot cadence).

If CloudLytics has any additional compliance requirements (e.g., EU DPA references, specific audit evidence), ask and we'll scope.

Marissa
Head of Compliance & Security
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this is very helpful and exactly what our procurement team needed. A couple quick follow-ups: 

- We'll accept the default 90-day retention for now but want the onboarding flag to be visible in the marketplace UI so our customers can select shorter windows. Can you add the sample UI copy?
- For deletion SLA please include the exact language we'll paste into our marketplace listing. Something like: "Full account data deletion (primary storage and audit-visible records) will be completed within 7 business days of verified request; backups will be purged within 30 days unless the account has elected extended snapshot retention." Does that align with Redwood's internal guarantees?

If yes, please send the final one-pager and I'll route to our procurement for sign-off. Also sending the DocuSign PO this afternoon.

Best,
Sophie
